P1: A construction site changes every hour. What happens is written into a site diary, from memory.
P2: Diary, P6 schedule, GAEB bill of quantities and claims live in separate tools, with no shared key. An observation never reaches the schedule or the contract.
P3: Tagwerk. Capture once on site, and it is linked to the schedule and the contract.
D1: The site manager picks the zone and sends one note. Speech goes through Whisper; typed, as here, counts the same.
D2: Tagwerk reads three facts: row A installed, two drywall workers sick, one defect.
D3: On the dashboard the capture arrives live. Progress is confirmed, the absence lands on its activity, and the forecast moves the finish two working days.
D4: Why? One click shows the cause, the contract position, and the recording behind it. Every percent traces back to a sentence.
D5: Underneath is one graph. Contract position, activity, place, recording, event. Each observation is linked at the moment it is captured, in Neo4j.
D6: One slider: past, today, forecast. Remaining work is re-simulated with the crews actually present.
D7: The camera alone only proposes. A tap or a sentence confirms. States only go up.
D8: The daily report writes itself, delays and causes included. The office gets exports for Primavera, GAEB and the calendar.
D9: With a BIM model, the same loop runs on over two thousand elements.
T1: Speech, vision and 3D run on one six-gigabyte GPU laptop. One project state, one graph, open exports. Tagwerk.
